reviewer: Claude Opus 5.5 (rubric-reviewer agent), scoring as Dr. Elena Vasquez
scope: Narration is the spoken > lines of s5_ai/script.md (8 scenes; sc3, sc4 and sc5 rewritten from the 2026-10-24 narration draft), with s4_analytics/script.md as the also story, where evidence caps a verdict at partial. Screen verdicts are judged on the 8 scenes of s5_ai/deck_anim.html and the eight qlik_panels/*.png they embed (unchanged since the last review), each opened and looked at, and on frames pulled from the re-rendered C:\Claude\MCG Demo\05_MCG_AI_Outcomes_1080p.mp4 (3:58.4: a 3 s opening sting, the 230.4 s body, a 5 s end sting), whose sc4 tile now reads '< 3.5 / Trust Score (out of 5) falls below threshold'.
note: Ingrid, the new lines answer three of my objections: preview is now said aloud for declarative pipelines and the MCP server, the Discovery Agent's alert goes to named owners, Henrik Jansen and Sophie Müller, on the same five-point Trust Score the tenant shows, and the MCP server is said to open our governed products to any compatible assistant. Four musts remain open: no scene shows an AI acting on our tenant, citations are asserted in this video but only demonstrated in story three, the agentic route is still labelled preview only in small print, and nobody approves generated sheets, the Data Product Agent's work or an outside assistant reading our products. It is better, but I would not yet sign this pillar off for the board or the NVWA.

verdicts.evidence: The sc1 panel is the Qlik Predict 'ML experiment' page on the live tenant: a model-metrics table of about thirty Logistic Regression, Gaussian Naive Bayes and LightGBM runs (best F1 0.144), SHAP importance for route_id, warehouse_id and battery_level_pct, and a ROC curve, captioned 'Qlik Predict - models trained on governed data, scored and compared'. In the re-rendered cut it is up from about 3.0 s to 7.5 s under the 'AI & Outcomes' title; as rendered the table figures are unreadable and the confusion-matrix and bias-detection blocks fall below the frame.
verdicts.gap: Nothing on screen changed in this cut. It is the analytics video's own panel (s4_analytics embeds the same v5_predict_coldchain.png), the narration over it never refers to it, and it shows models being trained, not an AI acting on governed data. No scene shows an Answers response with its citation, an agent conversation, the Discovery Agent's configuration or a coding-agent session, so the new sc5 claim that 'Answers cites the document behind every answer' plays over the glossary list, and sc4's 'What the Discovery Agent watches' is v3_dataquality.png, Qlik's stock semantic types, every one created by Qlik on Jul 29, 2025. The sc3 YAML diff and 'Problems: 0' chain are drawn HTML over v2_pipelines.png, whose two project cards (MCG Supply Chain Pipeline, olh_mcg_demo_cdc) are not the MCG Batch Pipeline the narration now calls 'a real task in our batch pipeline'. The only AI output on our own data is sc8's small-print 'Generated by AI on October 23, 2026 at 6:45 PM' over the Supply Chain Health description, with no reviewer shown. Seven of the eight panels are reused from stories one to three.

verdicts.evidence: Answers cites the document behind every answer
verdicts.gap: Video 05 now asserts the point but never demonstrates it: no answer is narrated, no source document is named, and the claim sits as one clause in a list under 'the same rule holds', so a viewer of this video alone hears a promise, not an answer that did not guess. The worked example, the NinjaVan contract amendment behind Singapore's fall to sixty-nine percent, exists only in the analytics narration, and no s5 panel is an Answers response. 'Every answer' is an absolute an auditor will test, with nothing shown to back it.

verdicts.evidence: opens these governed products to any MCP-compatible assistant, not only ours
verdicts.gap: The interoperability claim now lands. What remains: only 'these governed products' are named, not the quality metrics, lineage and catalog the server also exposes, and nothing says the governance travels with them, that an outside assistant sees only what its user is permitted to see and gets the trust score and draft status with the data. 'Not only ours' is ambiguous in a narration that also says 'our batch pipeline' and 'our address job': a viewer cannot tell whether 'ours' is Qlik's assistant or Meridian's. The clause trails a sentence that opens 'the same rule holds', so it reads as a human gate, which it is not.

verdicts.evidence: trust score falling below three and a half out of five, sync lag over an hour, volume moving more than fifty percent — and the alert goes to the product's owner: Henrik Jansen for Supply Chain Health, Sophie Müller for Last Mile
verdicts.gap: Thresholds and recipients are now both stated, and the sc4 tile shows the trust threshold on the same five-point scale as the closing 3.8 / 5. Residuals: 'A Discovery Agent can watch them' still leaves open whether the agent is configured on these products, and the sc4 panel shows no agent configuration, only Qlik's stock semantic types. The sc8 panel records Robert Schoenfeld, not Henrik Jansen, as the owner of Supply Chain Health, so the tenant contradicts the recipient the narration names. Nothing says what Henrik or Sophie is expected to do when the alert arrives.

verdicts.evidence: quality rules go live only when the data steward approves them
verdicts.gap: Gates are now named for four actions: the coding agent ('The human owns the decision'), glossary drafts ('wait for a human to approve them'), Data Quality Agent rules (the data steward) and low-confidence addresses (a human steward). Still ungated: the Data Product Agent packaging products, the generated sheets in the analytics video, where plain English 'can end up as a governed object in a governed app' with no reviewer, and the outside assistants the MCP server now opens our products to, with no one named who authorises that access. The 'consumption side' sentence borrows its only gate from quality rules, a build-side governance action, so no consumer-facing AI action has an approver. 'Except the one step that should stay human' still never says which step or whose. Approvers are 'a human' or a steward, never a role with sign-off authority. On screen, every glossary term in sc5 is Draft with the Stewards column empty, so the tenant shows no steward to approve anything.

Two of the preview capabilities are now said aloud in this video: declarative pipelines in sc3 and the Qlik MCP server ('also in preview') in sc5; sheet authoring over MCP is called preview only in the analytics video, and this video does not mention it. The Talend agentic route, which the route doc marks internal preview / roadmap, is narrated as working capability ('below it, here, to a human steward'); its only preview label is the sc6 footer 'Preview / roadmap', the small print the criterion excludes. Both spoken labels are parenthetical asides a viewer can miss.

verdicts.evidence: And the model can run in your own tenant.
verdicts.gap: Unchanged and now more exposed. Residency is said once, for the address route only, and as an option ('can run'), not as how Meridian runs it. Nothing says where customer data goes: 'the language model never leaves our infrastructure' is about the model, not the data, and is framed as what a buyer wants to hear. A Qlik Cloud tenant is hosted by Qlik, so 'your own tenant' and 'our infrastructure' are not the same thing. The new sc5 line opens the governed products to any MCP-compatible assistant, which for a third-party assistant means data leaving the tenant, and nothing says where it goes or under whose terms; nor where the coding agent, the governance agents or Answers send prompts and data.

verdicts.evidence: the build side produces trust, and the consumption side spends it.
verdicts.gap: Still mainly a slogan. The only new link is a trailing clause in sc5: an unnamed outside assistant, through a preview server, can reach 'these governed products'. Answers, the consumption surface this video names, is tied to documents ('cites the document behind every answer'), not to Supply Chain Health or Last Mile Performance, and nobody in this video uses a gold product to make a decision. The analytics video's worked decision, the APAC logistics lead changing the Singapore promise, rests on twenty-five operational documents, not on the gold products. A viewer is told that trust is spent but never sees who spends it, or on which product.

verdicts.evidence: The agent does the typing. The schema catches the mistakes. The human owns the decision. And if it is wrong, it is a git revert.
verdicts.gap: The narration is complete. The new 'a real task in our batch pipeline' is not borne out on screen: the YAML diff and schema check are drawn rather than captured, over two project cards that are not the MCG Batch Pipeline (the project name in mcg-batch-pipeline/qtcp_project.yaml), and the drawn diff omits the timeBasedScheduling/schedule nesting the real file has. The repo's MCG CRM Landing schedule.yaml still reads INTERVAL=15 ('every 15 minutes'), so there is no commit of the 30-minute change and no record of who approved it. 'The human' who owns the decision is never named.
